title: Mid-call hang-up (partial interview) has no outcome value and no data/resume policy
detail: A referee who answers, completes half the interview, then hangs up fits no enum value; verification exists only for 'completed', and no doc says whether partial answers are kept, scored, or trigger a re-attempt. The ~29% AI-refusal cohort makes mid-call abandonment common.
recommended_fix: Add a 'partial' outcome, define partial-verification capture, and state the resume/retry policy for abandoned calls.

title: Recommended web-form branch has no fraud-signal parity with the voice branch
evidence:
- **Lesson for us:** the industry standard is *cross-referencing digital exhaust*
  (IP/device/phone/email) between applicant and referee. For a voice-call product the
  analogs are: referee number line-type, referee number reused across applications,
  voice similarity, answer-template similarity.
detail: The recommended written-first design makes the form the completion engine ('(i) **complete the web form now** (mobile, no login — the Vitay/RefNow pattern)', fallback.md:350), yet the fraud stack covers only calls. Form links can be forwarded to a coached accomplice; the Xref/Refapp IP/device checks cited are never applied to the form path.
recommended_fix: Extend the layered stack with form-branch signals: submission IP/device vs applicant, link-open telemetry, completion latency.

title: Referee objection/STOP does not visibly short-circuit the fallback escalation chain
evidence:
+ one-sentence form offer; refusal honoured (Art 21), STOP across channels.
...
5. *Fallback:* form link + 2–3 reminders (48h) → applicant co-nudge (T+24h) → landlord warm
   handoff with attempt log (T+96h) → "unreachable" verdict (a real data point).
detail: Schema records "referee_channel_preference": "voice | form | none" (architecture.md:116), but neither fallback chain branches on objection: reminders, applicant co-nudge, and landlord warm handoff proceed unconditionally, inviting the landlord-controller to re-contact a referee who invoked Art 21.
recommended_fix: State that 'none'/STOP terminates all automated steps and flags the handoff so the landlord is told the referee objected.

title: wrong_number/invalid_number outcomes have no applicant-correction loop
evidence:
**Recommended precedence:** written-first contact (email+SMS with scheduling link and form option)
→ AI call at chosen/immediate slot → up to 2 more AI attempts (varied times) → web-form push with
reminders → landlord manual chase (warm handoff with attempt log) → "unreachable" verdict.
detail: The outcome enum includes wrong_number/invalid_number (architecture.md:70), but no step asks the applicant to verify/resupply the number. Retries would redial an uninvolved third party up to 3 times — someone who never received the Art 14 notice — and a wrong number is itself a fake-referee signal left unrouted.
recommended_fix: Route wrong/invalid-number outcomes to an immediate applicant number-confirmation step and stop further dials to that number.

title: Re-score consumption of non-completed call outcomes is undefined in the handoff contract
evidence:
triggered for shortlisted applicants → on completion, main app fires a *re-score*
...
  upgrades from letter-only assessment to call-grounded verification; its CategoryNote
detail: Only 'completed' carries a verification block (line 81); nullability of ai_summary, fraud_signals, and transcript for refused/no_answer/unreachable is unstated, and how reference_validator_agent should treat an 'unreachable' result (neutral, negative, or ignore) is never defined despite unreachable being called 'a real data point'.
recommended_fix: Specify field presence per outcome and define scoring semantics for each non-completed outcome in the v5 contract.

title: Employer references via switchboard/IVR/receptionist have no traversal path
detail: Employer referees frequently sit behind company switchboards, IVR menus, or receptionists. No document describes DTMF menu navigation, asking a gatekeeper for a named person, or scheduling via reception — the only non-human-answer handling described is AMD voicemail.
recommended_fix: Add an IVR/gatekeeper path to the call design (DTMF traversal or gatekeeper script) or restrict employer_ref to direct lines.

title: Recording-refusal branch is left as two undecided alternatives; transcript availability unstated
evidence: So: **announce recording at call start and honour a refusal** (stop recording or end call; offer the web form). This is a notice duty, not a consent requirement. **Confidence: High.**
detail: "recording_consent": "granted | declined | not_recorded" (architecture.md:115) anticipates unrecorded calls, but the docs never choose between continuing unrecorded vs ending the call, and never state whether transcript.turns[]/ai_summary exist for an unrecorded call (live STT without stored recording).
recommended_fix: Decide the refusal branch (recommend continue-unrecorded) and declare transcript/summary presence for recording_consent=declined.

title: Applicant attestation step has no negative branch
evidence:
1. *Application form:* applicant attests referees expect contact (new `reference_calling`
   consent type) — UX attestation, not an ePrivacy gate.
detail: The consent flow starts with the applicant attesting referees expect contact, but no document says what happens when the applicant declines the attestation — whether the application proceeds with manual referencing, form-only contact, or blocks.
recommended_fix: Define the decline branch: e.g. proceed form-only, or flag the application for manual reference handling.

title: Attempt accounting for the ≤3-retry policy is undefined (no-shows, busy, scheduled slots)
evidence:
with `attempt_count`, `next_attempt_at`, and terminal reasons. Retry policy (max 3,
  spread across business days/day-parts) lives in the agents service; the main app just
  renders state.
detail: Whether a booked-slot no-show, a busy signal, a wrong number, or an AMD voicemail each consume one of the ≤3 attempts — and whether rescheduling resets the counter — is never specified, so retry-exhaustion timing (and the T+96h handoff trigger) is indeterminate.
recommended_fix: Define which outcomes decrement attempt_count and how scheduled-slot no-shows and reschedules interact with the cap.

title: AMD misclassification path is unhandled though the flow branches on AMD
evidence: statement. AMD voicemail: short message pointing to the link in the SMS.
detail: The orchestration uses answering-machine detection to choose between a voicemail message and the live AI conversation, but no document addresses AMD error: a human greeted with the voicemail message, or a voicemail box getting the interactive agent.
recommended_fix: Specify behaviour on AMD uncertainty (e.g. default to live agent with a disclosure-first line) and log AMD confidence per attempt.

title: language_barrier outcome exists with no handling path anywhere
evidence: "outcome": "completed | voicemail | no_answer | busy | refused | wrong_number | invalid_number | declined_ai | language_barrier",
detail: The schema anticipates language barriers, but neither the consent flow nor the fallback chain mentions multilingual support — no translated SMS/form, no language-selection on call, no routing for referees who cannot complete an English AI call.
recommended_fix: Either scope v1 to English and document that, or add a translated-form fallback for language_barrier outcomes.

title: Within-application cross-slot number reuse (same number as landlord AND employer ref) is not covered
evidence: | Number reuse | same referee number across multiple applications | our DB | any reuse under different referee names → hard flag |
detail: The reuse signal checks across applications, and contact_duplicate_of_applicant (architecture.md:99) checks the applicant's own number. The classic fake — one friend supplied as both landlord_ref and employer_ref on the same application — matches neither check and is never listed as a signal.
recommended_fix: Add a within-application cross-slot duplicate-number check to the v1 pre-call layer.
